c.tagline: Historic Ghanaian coastal city anchored by a UNESCO slave-trade fortress and golden Atlantic beaches.

taxi.fareNote: Shared taxis and tro-tros are cheap but unmetered; agree on a fare before you get in. Private taxis for tourists should also be negotiated up front.

emergency.note: The unified national emergency line 112 also connects to police, fire, and ambulance services; response times outside Accra can be slow.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Victoria Park: Jubilee Park & Cape Coast Methodist Cathedral

avoid.reason: Beaches after dark and persistent self-appointed 'guides' or friendship-bracelet hustlers around the castle deserve extra awareness.

hood_desc: The civic heart of Cape Coast, centered on Victoria Park and the old colonial-era buildings lining Commercial Street; the easiest base for reaching the castle, the market, and onward transport.
Home to Cape Coast Castle, the UNESCO-listed fortress central to the transatlantic slave trade, and the fishing harbor beside it, lined with pastel colonial buildings and busy fishing canoes.
The city's largest and liveliest market, rebuilt in recent years, where traders sell cloth, produce, and fresh fish; a good place to see everyday Cape Coast life.
A quieter residential suburb inland from the historic center, popular with families and increasingly with guesthouses catering to volunteers and students.
Home to the University of Cape Coast, with a younger, livelier feel thanks to student bars, cheap eats, and a beachfront campus.

water.note: Drink bottled or sealed sachet water rather than tap.

transit.hours: Roughly 5am-8pm, with limited service after dark
transit.pay: Cash only, paid directly to the driver or mate
transit.map: No official transit map; routes are learned locally
transit.note: No public bus network or metro; tro-tros and shared or private taxis are the main way to get around.

bus: STC and VIP long-distance buses connect Cape Coast to Accra, Takoradi, and Kumasi

tip.r: 5-10% at tourist-oriented restaurants is appreciated; not expected at small local eateries. Guides at Cape Coast Castle and Kakum National Park often expect a modest tip.
